newsitem.title: FINLAND: Cultor down sharply as result disappoints.
newsitem.headline: Cultor down sharply as result disappoints.

text.p: Shares in Finnish foodstuffs and animal feed group Cultor Oy fell over five percent on Wednesday after a 42 percent slide in its Jan-Aug profits was bigger than feared despite an earlier profit-warning, brokers said.
At 1155/0855 GMT, the liquid Cultor series 2 traded at 230.00, down 14.00 markka or almost six percent but volume was thin at less than three million markka.
The little traded Cultor series 1 was 1.00 markka up at 239.00 only due to one in-house deal which did not reflect external matters, brokers said.
Cultor's January-August profit after financial items was 196 million markka compared a 231 million markka median of analysts' forecasts, which ranged from 197 to 300 million markka.

"It is quite dramatic that you give a warning and then do not even reach the lowest forecast," one analyst said, adding that the fall was more due to Cultor's January-August result than Cultor's outlook. He said this did not look too bad.
However, it was clear that Cultor's business had become more risky and its results more volatile after the company started investing in higher levels of refinement in its products, the analyst said.
